subject: Physics
subtopic: Fluid statics, buoyancy and Bernoulli flow
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate. It is never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic, while practice percentages only route support.

rungs.aha: In a fluid at rest, pressure is a scalar acting normal to surfaces and increases with depth because deeper points support more fluid above.
learner_owns: Can distinguish force from area and can compare vertical depth below a free surface.
must_contain: A vessel with several differently oriented pressure arrows at the same depth, all normal to their local surfaces.
Two points at different depths but in the same connected static fluid.

misconception.wrong_idea: Pressure at a point in a fluid has one preferred direction, downward because of gravity.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: At one point in still water, would a tiny vertical surface and a tiny horizontal surface experience pressure in different directions relative to themselves?
misconception.repair: Pressure is scalar; the force it produces on a surface is normal to that surface. Depth changes its magnitude, not a preferred pressure-vector direction.

rungs.closure: Given points at equal and unequal depths in a connected static fluid, rank their pressures and draw the force direction on differently oriented small surfaces.

controlled_variation.notice: pressure magnitude is unchanged while the surface force stays normal to each surface

controlled_variation.hold: fluid density, gravity, and surface pressure
controlled_variation.notice: pressure increases with vertical depth regardless of container shape

engineering_dependencies.reason: Static-fluid pressure versus depth needs gate-owned conditions.

must_contain: An object outline with the displaced-fluid volume highlighted separately from the object's total volume.
Equal-mass objects of different volumes fully submerged in the same fluid.

controlled_variation.vary: object volume at fixed full submersion
controlled_variation.notice: buoyant force changes with displaced volume even when object mass is held fixed

must_contain: A directed flow path through wide and narrow sections with velocity arrows and cross-sectional areas marked.
Equal time intervals showing equal fluid volume crossing each section.

controlled_variation.notice: velocity arrows lengthen where the area narrows

must_contain: Two marked points on the same streamline with pressure, speed, and height terms shown as one energy ledger.
A horizontal narrowing case followed by a case where height also changes.

controlled_variation.vary: cross-sectional area on a horizontal streamline
controlled_variation.hold: fluid density, height, and steady ideal-flow conditions
controlled_variation.notice: narrowing raises speed and lowers static pressure in this controlled case

controlled_variation.hold: same streamline, fluid density, and steady ideal-flow conditions
controlled_variation.notice: pressure cannot be inferred from speed change alone when gravitational term also changes

rungs.aha: Bernoulli applications such as efflux and Venturi measurements are solved by choosing comparison points whose equal terms can be justified, then combining continuity and energy rather than memorizing a special formula.
learner_owns: Bernoulli trades pressure, kinetic, and gravitational terms only under its stated ideal-flow conditions.
Can use continuity to relate speeds at two sections.
must_contain: A tank-to-orifice directed path with free-surface and exit points explicitly chosen.
A Venturi with pressure taps and areas marked before any algebraic cancellation.

misconception.wrong_idea: Torricelli's speed sqrt(2gh) applies to any fluid leaving any opening regardless of tank size or pressure conditions.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: If the tank cross-section is not much larger than the outlet, can the free-surface speed still be treated as zero?
misconception.repair: Derive the simplification from chosen points and continuity; only neglect a term when the geometry or boundary conditions justify it.

rungs.closure: Given a tank or Venturi setup, choose the two comparison points, name every term that cancels and why, and identify any approximation used.

controlled_variation.vary: outlet area relative to tank area
controlled_variation.hold: fluid, height difference, and equal atmospheric pressures
controlled_variation.notice: surface speed becomes negligible only in the small-outlet limit

controlled_variation.hold: steady incompressible flow and fixed section areas
controlled_variation.notice: the measured pressure difference maps to the speed difference only after continuity links the section speeds

engineering_dependencies.reason: Continuity must be gate-owned before combining it with an energy relation.
Bernoulli's ideal-flow ledger needs gate-owned applicability conditions.
Tank and Venturi numerical exits need an implemented coupled validator.

family.invariant_demand: Choose the fluid model and comparison points, follow one connected static region or streamline as appropriate, keep pressure, speed, height, and displaced volume distinct, and verify the result with conservation and limiting cases.
family.difficult_move: Selecting the physically comparable points and deciding which quantities are actually conserved or equal before cancelling terms.
family.independent_check: Test a limiting case: equal depths recover equal static pressure, equal areas recover equal flow speed, and removing a height or speed difference must remove its corresponding Bernoulli contribution.

support_ladder.handed_over: The fluid regime and comparison points are identified, with candidate equal terms marked; the learner justifies cancellations, computes, and checks.
The relevant points or control sections are marked, but the learner decides the governing relation and equalities.
Only the apparatus or flow description and measured values are given.

transfer.changed_demand: Oil flows through a long narrow tube with a substantial pressure loss: decide whether ideal Bernoulli between distant points is an adequate model.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether viscous dissipation can be neglected over the stated flow path

transfer.changed_demand: A velocity-arrow field and pressure labels replace the pipe-area numbers; infer where continuity predicts narrowing or widening.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the cross-sectional-area changes implied by the arrow-field speed pattern

transfer.changed_demand: A draining tank has an outlet comparable in area to the tank; determine efflux speed without neglecting free-surface motion.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the need to retain the free-surface speed and relate it to outlet speed by continuity

transfer.changed_demand: An oddly shaped submerged body replaces spheres and blocks; determine how buoyant force changes as only part of it emerges.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the displaced-fluid volume at the new immersion state
